AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where should the graft joint of a grafted seedling be? (1 mark)
   A. Above the ground
   B. Deep below the soil
   C. In the compost
   D. In water

2. How should the seedling be removed from its polythene bag? (1 mark)
   A. By pulling the stem hard
   B. By cutting the roots
   C. Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   D. By throwing it

3. Why do we weed around fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Weeds give fruits
   B. Weeds protect the stem
   C. Weeds take water and food from the plants
   D. Weeds add sugar

4. What is a fruit? (1 mark)
   A. The roots of a plant
   B. The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   C. The stem of a plant
   D. The leaves of a plant

5. What is leather made from? (1 mark)
   A. Eggs
   B. Feathers
   C. Wool only
   D. Animal hides and skins

6. Which product does a dairy cow give? (1 mark)
   A. Eggs
   B. Feathers
   C. Milk
   D. Wool

7. What is the meat from cattle called? (1 mark)
   A. Pork
   B. Beef
   C. Chicken
   D. Mutton

8. Which domestic animal is often kept in dry areas for milk and meat? (1 mark)
   A. Duck
   B. Rabbit
   C. Pig
   D. Camel

9. Which of these is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar
   B. Cooking oil
   C. Sukuma wiki
   D. Ugali

10. Which food group gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Energy-giving foods
   B. Salt
   C. Water only
   D. Protective foods only

11. What does proportion mean in a meal? (1 mark)
   A. The right amount of each kind of food
   B. The colour of the food
   C. The price of the food
   D. The number of plates

12. Which of these belongs to more than one group? (1 mark)
   A. Groundnuts
   B. Salt
   C. Water
   D. Sugar

13. Which food is usually shallow fried? (1 mark)
   A. Boiled rice
   B. Eggs
   C. Tea
   D. Boiled maize

14. What should be done with a fire after cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it burning
   B. Add more wood
   C. Put it out or switch off the gas
   D. Cover it with paper

15. Which of these foods needs a long time of boiling before it is soft enough to eat? (1 mark)
   A. Cucumber
   B. Tomato
   C. Ripe banana
   D. Dry beans

16. Why do we cook food? (1 mark)
   A. To make it dirty
   B. To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   C. To make it disappear
   D. To make it colder

17. Which disease can result from drinking unsafe water? (1 mark)
   A. A cut
   B. Toothache
   C. Sunburn
   D. Cholera

18. Why should you bathe every day? (1 mark)
   A. To waste water
   B. To make skin dry
   C. To make the body hot
   D. To remove sweat, dirt and germs

19. Why should we wear shoes? (1 mark)
   A. To make us tall
   B. To hide our feet
   C. To be heavier
   D. To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers

20. Which part is often forgotten when washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. The elbows only
   B. The knees
   C. Under the nails and between the fingers
   D. Only the palms

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how mulch and compost help a young fruit tree. (4 marks)

22. Explain pruning. (2 marks)

23. Describe how to make a tippy tap. (4 marks)

24. Give three times when you should wash your hands. (3 marks)

25. Write the steps for preparing a meal using both boiling and shallow frying. Include hygiene and safety. (5 marks)

26. Explain four ways germs can enter the body. (4 marks)

27. Why should you brush teeth twice a day? (2 marks)

28. Explain the difference between domestic and wild animals. (2 marks)

29. Describe how to prepare a planting hole for a fruit tree. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Above the ground
   Buried joints can rot or grow roots of the wrong kind.

2. C — Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   Broken roots harm the seedling.

3. C — Weeds take water and food from the plants
   Weeds compete with the crop.

4. B — The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds.

5. D — Animal hides and skins
   Skins of cattle, goats and sheep become leather.

6. C — Milk
   Dairy cows are kept for milk.

7. B — Beef
   Beef comes from cattle.

8. D — Camel
   Camels survive in dry regions.

9. C — Sukuma wiki
   Vegetables give vitamins and minerals.

10. A — Energy-giving foods
   Carbohydrates and fats give energy.

11. A — The right amount of each kind of food
   Proportion means the right amounts.

12. A — Groundnuts
   Groundnuts give protein and energy.

13. B — Eggs
   Eggs are commonly fried in a pan.

14. C — Put it out or switch off the gas
   This prevents accidents and saves fuel.

15. D — Dry beans
   Dry beans are hard and need long cooking.

16. B — To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   Heat kills germs and softens food.

17. D — Cholera
   Cholera spreads through dirty water.

18. D — To remove sweat, dirt and germs
   Bathing keeps the body clean.

19. D — To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers
   Shoes protect the feet.

20. C — Under the nails and between the fingers
   Germs hide there.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mulch keeps the soil moist, reduces weeds and protects roots from heat. Compost feeds the tree and improves soil structure.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for mulch, 2 marks for compost.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is cutting off dead, weak or crossing branches so that light and air can reach the plant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cutting, 1 mark for the purpose.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Take a clean jerrican; make a small hole near the cap; hang it; tie a string from the cap to a foot lever; place a basin below and hang soap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before eating, after using the toilet, after playing outside, after touching animals, after coughing (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands; wash food; boil potatoes until soft; shallow fry an egg or fish; serve with vegetables; safety: adult present, handles inward, dry cloth, water away from hot oil; clean up after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for hygiene, 1 for boiling, 1 for frying, 1 for safety, 1 for serving and cleaning.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Through the mouth from dirty hands, dirty food, dirty water, and through cuts or feet without shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: It removes food and germs that cause decay and keeps the mouth fresh.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for removing food, 1 mark for preventing decay.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Domestic animals are kept and cared for by people. Wild animals live freely in nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a sunny site; dig a hole about half a metre wide and deep; put topsoil aside; mix topsoil with compost; put some mixture back in the hole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.
